PURPOSE: THE PURPOSE OF THIS GRANT IS TO DEVELOP MACHINE LEARNING METHODS THAT ALLOW MANUFACTURING ROBOTS TO QUICKLY BE ADAPTED TO PERFORM NEW TASKS USING VISION AND TOUCH SENSING. THIS WILL ESTABLISH WAYS FOR THESE LEARNING METHODS TO BE MORE EASILY ADOPTED BY US MANUFACTURERS. ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED: THIS PROPOSAL WILL INCLUDE THREE ACTIVITIES:ACTIVITY 1 - SELF-SUPERVISED VISION-BASED OBJECT MANIPULATION - THE ROBOTICS TRAINING CENTER WILL TEACH ROBOTS HOW TO TRANSFORM ARBITRARY OBJECTS INTO TARGET POSES. THIS IS USEFUL FOR ASSEMBLY TASKS FOR INDUSTRIAL ROBOTS, IN WHICH THE MANUFACTURING ROBOT NEEDS TO PLACE OBJECTS INTO TARGET POSITIONS. ACTIVITY 2 - VIBROTACTILE SENSING FOR MONITORING ASSEMBLY PROCESSES - EXPLORE THE USE OF VIBROTACTILE DATA FOR MONITORING MANUFACTURING ASSEMBLY PROCESSES TO DETERMINE WHEN AN ASSEMBLY STEP IS COMPLETE OR AN ERROR HAS OCCURRED. ACTIVITY 3 - INTEGRATION AND DEVELOPMENT OF A DIGITAL BACKBONE FOR LARGE-SCALE DATA COLLECTION AND PROCESSING IN ROBOTICS TRAINING - WILL FOCUS ON THE INTEGRATION OF THE ROBOTICS TRAINING CENTER WITH THE MILL 19A DIGITAL BACKBONE AND DATA HISTORIAN. EXPECTED OUTCOMES: THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL HELP MAKE MANUFACTURING INDUSTRIES MORE COMPETITIVE AND ROBUST TO CHANGES IN MARKETS AND SUPPLY CHAINS.INTENDED BENEFICIARIES: ROBOT VENDORS, ROBOT END USERS, ROBOT MANUFACTURERS, U.S. INDUSTRY, ROBOT SYSTEMS INTEGRATORS.SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES: THE RECIPIENT INTENDS TO HAVE A SUBAWARD TO THE ADVANCED ROBOTICS FOR MANUFACTURING (ARM) INSTITUTE, WHO WILL PUBLICIZE THE TECHNOLOGY AND DOCUMENTATION THAT WILL BE DEVELOPED BY THIS ROBOTICS TRAINING CENTER AND MAKE IT AVAILABLE TO THEIR MEMBERS FOR INCORPORATION INTO OR ADDITION TO  ANY OF THEIR ROUGHLY 16,000 ROBOTICS-FOR-MANUFACTURING TRAINING PROGRAMS.

THE ABILITY TO PLACE GRAPHENE, A SINGLE LAYER OF CARBON ATOMS IN SPECIFIC LOCATIONS ON FAB-FRIENDLY SUBSTRATES IS CRITICAL AS A COMPONENT IN FUTURE ELECTRONIC AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGIES.ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED:THE TECHNICAL APPROACH WILL CONSIST OF 3 TASKS, NAMELY INITIAL FEA MODELING, CHARACTERIZATION OF ADHESION ENERGIES AT RELEVANT INTERFACES, FOLLOWED BY PROOF-OF-CONCEPT EXPERIMENTS (I.E., VALIDATION OF THE TECHNOLOGY ON SUBSTRATE SIZES OF 1? X 1?).  FURTHERMORE, A FOLLOW-UP PLAN TO SCALE UP THE TECHNOLOGY HAS BEEN DEVELOPED. TITLE: CMU/NIST AI MEASUREMENT SCIENCE & ENGINEERING COOPERATIVE RESEARCH CENTERPURPOSE: ESTABLISH THE CMU/NIST AI MEASUREMENT SCIENCE & ENGINEERING COOPERATIVE RESEARCH CENTER (AIMSEC) TO FACILITATE COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH AND EXPERIMENTATION FOCUSED ON ADVANCING OUR NATIONAL CAPABILITY FOR TEST AND EVALUATION OF MODERN AI CAPABILITIES AND TOOLS. THERE ARE THREE PRINCIPAL GOALS: 1. ADVANCE MODERN AI RISK MANAGEMENT 2. VALIDATE EVALUATION APPROACHES THROUGH STAKEHOLDER PARTNERSHIPS. 3. TRANSLATE ASSESSMENT CAPABILITIES AND METHODOLOGIES TO PRACTICE. RESEARCH WILL FOCUS ON ADVANCING MEASUREMENT SCIENCE FOR MODERN AI SYSTEMS, INCLUDING MACHINE LEARNING (ML) AND GENERATIVE AI (GENAI) SYSTEMS, SUCH AS LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS (LLMS). ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED: CREATE A PRACTICAL TAXONOMY OF THREATS AGAINST LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS (LLMS). THE PROPOSED WORK INCLUDES DEVELOPING TECHNIQUES TO REDUCE MEMORIZATION AND PROTECT CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION PROVABLY, EVEN IF IT RESULTS IN LESS EXACT OUTPUTS. DEVELOP NEW MEASURES OF ROBUSTNESS FOR ML MODELS THAT BETTER REFLECT A MODEL?S ABILITY TO WITHSTAND ATTACKS IN PRACTICAL SCENARIOS. DEVELOP RICHER DEFINITIONS OF ALIGNMENT, CORRECTNESS, AND INTENT TO DETERMINE THE SUITABILITY OF GENERATIVE AI SYSTEMS FOR THEIR INTENDED USES. CREATE A STATE-OF-THE-ART SUITE OF ATTACKS AGAINST LLMS FOR TESTING NEW MODELS. THESE ACTIVITIES WILL BE ORGANIZED IN THREE STREAMS OF EFFORT ALIGNED WITH NIST AI PRIORITIES.  -	VALIDITY, RELIABILITY, SAFETY, PRIVACY, AND SECURITY-	ACCOUNTABILITY, TRANSPARENCY, FAIRNESS, AND EXPLAINABILITY-	GENERATIVE AI EVALUATIONEXPECTED OUTCOMES: DEVELOPMENT OF AI SYSTEM-LEVEL TOOLING, METRICS, EVALUATION PROCEDURES, DEVELOPMENT PROCESSES, AND BEST PRACTICES TO ENSURE AI SYSTEM BUILDERS CONSISTENTLY ENGINEER SAFE AI SYSTEMS. GOALS ARE TO ADVANCE MODERN AI RISK MANAGEMENT, VALIDATE EVALUATION APPROACHES THROUGH STAKEHOLDER PARTNERSHIPS, AND TRANSLATE ASSESSMENT CAPABILITIES AND METHODOLOGIES TO PRACTICE. PURPOSE: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) IS WIDESPREAD IN TODAY'S SOCIETY, WITH AI ALGORITHMS BEING INCREASINGLY RELIED ON TO MAKE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISIONS ABOUT INDIVIDUALS. ALTHOUGH THERE WAS INITIAL OPTIMISM THAT AI APPLICATIONS WOULD MAKE A MORE EFFICIENT AND FAIR SOCIETY, ANECDOTAL EXAMPLES OF BIASED OUTCOMES IN AI APPLICATIONS NOW ABOUND FROM DOMAINS AS WIDE AS WEB SEARCH, MACHINE TRANSLATION, UNIVERSITY ADMISSIONS, RESUME SCREENING, AND JOB CANDIDATE ASSESSMENT. YET, BEYOND THESE ANECDOTES, THERE REMAINS NO COMPREHENSIVE STUDY THAT EXAMINES (1) HOW THE EXTENT OF BIASES IN GENERAL-PURPOSE MODALITY REPRESENTATIONS THAT AI RELIES ON PROPAGATE TO DOWNSTREAM DECISIONS, (2) HOW BIASED AI DECISIONS INTERACT WITH THE BIASES OF HUMANS-IN-THE-LOOP, AND (3) HOW AI-MEDIATED OUTCOMES IMPACT THE BIASES OF FUTURE GENERATIONS OF AI MODELS. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH SEEKS TO ADDRESS THESE NEEDS, THEREBY CONTRIBUTING TO NIST'S TRUSTWORTHY AND RESPONSIBLE AI EFFORTS. ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED: IN THIS PROJECT, THE PROPOSERS WILL ANALYZE THE IMPACT OF BIASED GENERAL-PURPOSE MACHINE REPRESENTATIONS GENERATED VIA UNSUPERVISED MACHINE LEARNING ON THE AUTOMATED DECISIONS OF SUPERVISED MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS THAT RELY ON STRUCTURED DATA IN THE EMPLOYMENT DOMAIN. AS A STARTING POINT, THE PROPOSERS WILL FOCUS ON GENDER AND RACIAL BIAS IN RESUME SCREENING AND JOB CANDIDATE ASSESSMENT, AN APPLICATION DOMAIN WITH CLEAR CONSEQUENCES FOR LIFE'S OPPORTUNITIES AND OUTCOMES. THE PROPOSERS WILL DEVELOP A BIAS PROPAGATION AND INTERACTION AUDIT FRAMEWORK THAT GENERALIZES ACROSS MODALITIES, BIAS TYPES, AND APPLICATION DOMAINS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES: THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL CONDUCT TWO COMPLEMENTARY STUDIES TO ANSWER THE FOLLOWING IMPORTANT QUESTIONS: (1) GIVEN THAT BIAS REFLECTED FROM SOCIETY TO LARGE-SCALE DATASETS GETS EMBEDDED IN GENERAL-PURPOSE MACHINE REPRESENTATIONS USED FOR PROCESSING DATA, HOW DOES REPRESENTATIONAL BIAS PROPAGATE TO DOWNSTREAM APPLICATIONS? (2) HOW ARE HUMANS-IN-THE-LOOP COLLABORATING WITH AI IN DECISION MAKING AFFECTED BY THE BIASED OUTCOMES OF MACHINES,GIVEN THEIR OWN IMPLICIT BIASES? THE RESEARCH STUDIES SUPPORTED BY THIS GRANT WILL BE PUBLISHED IN THE SCIENTIFIC LITERATURE, SPECIFICALLY BY CONTRIBUTING PAPERS ON AN ANNUAL BASIS AT ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND FAIRNESS VENUES FOR COMPUTER AND INFORMATION SCIENCES. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES: SOCIOTECHNICAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) SYSTEMS WITH HUMANS-IN-THE-LOOP MAKE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISIONS ABOUT INDIVIDUALS IN SCENARIOS THAT DETERMINE LIFE'S OPPORTUNITIES AND OUTCOMES. DEVELOPING METHODS AND METRICS TO MEASURE HOW THE BIASES OF SOCIETY, AI, AND HUMANS-IN-THE-LOOP INTERACT IN DECISION MAKING WILL PROVIDE QUANTITATIVE EVIDENCE ON THE IMPACT OF AI ON SOCIETY. THIS PROJECT WILL BENEFIT THE GENERAL PUBLIC BY PROVIDING MUCH-NEEDED RESEARCH TO SUPPORT DEVELOPING STANDARDS FOR IDENTIFYING AND MANAGING BIAS IN AI. FAIR WITH HARMFUL BIAS MANAGED IS A KEY CHARACTERISTIC OF TRUSTWORTHY AI AS DEFINED IN NIST'S AI RISK MANAGEMENT FRAMEWORK, THEREFORE THIS BIAS RESEARCH WILL CLEARLY BENEFIT NIST'S LARGER TRUSTWORTHY AND RESPONSIBLE AI PROGRAM AND ADVANCE THE STATE-OF-THE-ART FOR BIAS EVALUATIONS IN AI SYSTEMS. SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES: THERE ARE NO PLANNED SUBAWARDS.
